name: Order-Free Boolean Recognition of the Dismantlable-Ample Forbidden Basis
statement: Let an irredundantly embedded binary family $H$ be presented by a signing of the minimal nonfaces of a proposed shattered complex. Then $H$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor for the dismantlable ample classes exactly when the signing is admissible, $H$ admits no acyclic trace-carrier scheme, and each of its $3|F|$ one-coordinate restrictions and contractions admits such a scheme for its own shattered complex. Together with the antipodally twice-punctured cubes $Q_n^{--}$ for $n\ge3$, these signed presentations modulo coordinate permutations and reorientations form the full forbidden basis. The conditions use only finite trace-fiber data of $H$ and its explicit elementary images.
proof: The fixed-shadow signed-clutter theorem identifies admissibility with ampleness and fixes the shattered complex. The first-loss and trace-carrier theorems identify absence of a scheme with nonpeelability and existence of schemes on the elementary images with their peelability. Descendant-free pc-minor reduction makes those elementary tests equivalent to pc-minimality and supplies the quotient by cube symmetries. The nonample-layer theorem supplies exactly the antipodally twice-punctured cubes.
comments: This is an exact static recognition criterion. It does not satisfy the manuscript's stronger goal of a noncircular generative classification, because scheme existence is equivalent to corner peelability.
